newsitem.title: MEXICO: Ex-Mexican lawman denies drug cartel link.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Mexican lawman denies drug cartel link.

text.p: A former Mexican deputy attorney general denied on Wednesday that he had been bought off by drug cartels.
Javier Coello Trejo said in an exclusive interview with Mexico's TV network Televisa that he was inocent and had no links with drug cartels.
"I feel innocent, I am innocent, I have peace of mind," Coello Trejo said. "I have had no links with ... drug traffickers," he said in the interview from his office.
The Miami Herald said on Sunday that Coello Trejo was named by Juan Carlos Ramirez Abadia, a jailed Cali drug cartel kingpin, as having been bought off by the Colombian ring.

Ramirez, in sworn testimony to Mexican prosecutors on April 7 and 8, said cocaine shipments through Mexico were protected by Coello Trejo and Guillermo Gonzalez Calderoni, a former Judicial Police Commander.
"Coello Trejo ... permitted the activities of the cartels and they paid him for this," the newspaper said Ramirez told prosecutors, citing parts of 12-pages of sworn testimony.

The allegations were the latest in a series of charges against Coello Trejo and Gonzalez Calderoni, who left their posts amid accusations by the Mexican government that they had ties to drug traffickers. Gonzalez Calderoni has also denied the allegations.

In October, a former Mexican police commander who joined the Gulf Cartel testified in the Houston, Texas, trial of drug cartel chieftain Juan Garcia Abrego that bribes totalling $1.5 million a month were paid to Coello Trejo and two other officials for protection.

Ramirez turned himself in to Colombian authorities in March 1996, following the lead of other Cali cartel chiefs. he was convicted of drug trafficking in Cali in November and sentenced to more than 13 years in prision.
